```{r}
#| label: setup

library(tidyverse)
library(gt)
library(scales)
library(showtext)
# library(highcharter)

# The classic tips dataset used by the original bslib theme demo app
tips <- read_csv(
  "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mwaskom/seaborn-data/master/tips.csv",
  show_col_types = FALSE
) |>
  mutate(
    day = factor(day, levels = c("Thur", "Fri", "Sat", "Sun")),
    time = factor(time, levels = c("Lunch", "Dinner")),
    tip_pct = tip / total_bill
  )
```

```{r}
#| label: brand-theme

# ---- Read _brand.yml (searches the project dir for it) ----------------------
brand <- brand.yml::read_brand_yml()

# Resolve a color: a palette name (e.g. "blue") -> hex, or pass a hex through
palette <- brand$color$palette
resolve_color <- function(x, default) {
  if (is.null(x)) {
    return(default)
  }
  if (!is.null(palette[[x]])) palette[[x]] else x
}

brand_cols <- list(
  fg = resolve_color(brand$color$foreground, "#222222"),
  bg = resolve_color(brand$color$background, "#FFFFFF"),
  primary = resolve_color(brand$color$primary, "#2780E3"),
  secondary = resolve_color(brand$color$secondary, "#6C757D"),
  success = resolve_color(brand$color$success, "#3FB618"),
  info = resolve_color(brand$color$info, "#9954BB"),
  warning = resolve_color(brand$color$warning, "#FF7518"),
  danger = resolve_color(brand$color$danger, "#FF0039")
)

# Categorical scale built from the brand's theme colors
brand_discrete <- unname(unlist(
  brand_cols[c("primary", "secondary", "success", "info", "warning", "danger")]
))

# ---- Fonts: use the brand's base font via Google Fonts if possible ----------
base_family <- brand$typography$base$family
if (!is.null(base_family)) {
  try(sysfonts::font_add_google(base_family), silent = TRUE)
  showtext_auto()
  showtext_opts(dpi = 200)
} else {
  base_family <- ""
}

# ---- A ggplot theme that uses the brand ------------------------------------
theme_brand <- function(base_size = 9) {
  theme_minimal(base_size = base_size, base_family = base_family) +
    theme(
      text = element_text(color = brand_cols$fg),
      plot.background = element_rect(fill = brand_cols$bg, color = NA),
      panel.background = element_rect(fill = brand_cols$bg, color = NA),
      panel.grid.major = element_line(color = alpha(brand_cols$fg, 0.12)),
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
      axis.title = element_text(color = brand_cols$fg),
      axis.text = element_text(color = alpha(brand_cols$fg, 0.75)),
      legend.title = element_blank(),
      legend.position = "top",
      legend.text = element_text(color = brand_cols$fg)
    )
}

theme_set(theme_brand())
update_geom_defaults("point", list(colour = brand_cols$primary))
update_geom_defaults("smooth", list(colour = brand_cols$warning))
```

## Overview

As bills grow larger, tips grow with them, but not perfectly proportionally —
the curve flattens a little at the high end, suggesting the biggest checks
don't always earn a tip that keeps pace percentage-wise.

```{r}
#| label: fig-bill-vs-tip
#| fig-cap: "Total bill vs. tip, with a loess trend line"

loess_fit <- loess(tip ~ total_bill, data = tips)
loess_line <- tibble(
  total_bill = seq(min(tips$total_bill), max(tips$total_bill), length.out = 100)
) |>
  mutate(tip = predict(loess_fit, total_bill))

ggplot(tips, aes(total_bill, tip)) +
  geom_point(size = 1.8, alpha = 0.6, color = brand_cols$primary) +
  geom_smooth(
    method = "loess",
    formula = y ~ x,
    se = FALSE,
    color = brand_cols$warning,
    linewidth = 1
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = label_dollar()) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = label_dollar()) +
  labs(x = "Total bill ($)", y = "Tip ($)")
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-tips-data
#| tbl-cap: "First 10 recorded checks"

tips |>
  slice_head(n = 10) |>
  select(total_bill, tip, sex, smoker, day, time, size) |>
  gt() |>
  fmt_currency(columns = c(total_bill, tip), decimals = 2) |>
  cols_label(
    total_bill = "Total bill",
    tip = "Tip",
    sex = "Sex",
    smoker = "Smoker",
    day = "Day",
    time = "Time",
    size = "Party size"
  ) |>
  # opt_table_font(font = google_font("Inter")) |>
  tab_options(
    table.width = pct(100),
    column_labels.font.weight = "bold"
  )
```

## Tip percentages by day

How tip percentage is distributed across
each day of the week:

```{r}
#| label: fig-tip-pct-ridge
#| fig-cap: "Distribution of tip percentage by day"

ggplot(tips, aes(tip_pct, fill = day, color = day)) +
  geom_density(alpha = 0.4, linewidth = 0.6) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = brand_discrete) +
  scale_color_manual(values = brand_discrete) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = label_percent()) +
  labs(x = "Tip percentage", y = "Density")
```
